findings.title: enableSqlExpressions() is dead logic that always returns false
findings.body: `enableSqlExpressions` computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` and then returns `false` on both branches, so the feature-toggle lookup has no effect and the function is a constant `false`. Besides being unreachable/dead code (which some linters such as `unparam`/`gocritic` will flag and which can fail CI), the inverted condition reads like a mistake: a future reader may "fix" the inversion and accidentally re-enable the code path this PR is meant to kill. If the intent is to hard-disable SQL expressions, the function should be a plain `return false` (or the branch removed entirely) with a comment referencing CVE-2024-9264 explaining why the toggle is deliberately ignored.

findings.title: Disabled SQL expressions produce inconsistent, misleading error messages
findings.body: The new guard returns `sqlExpressions is not implemented` for the typed-query path, while the legacy path (`UnmarshalSQLCommand` -> `NewSQLCommand` -> `sql.TablesList`, which now hits the stubbed `RunCommands` returning `not implemented`) surfaces `error reading SQL command` (pkg/expr/sql_command.go:34) and the execute path surfaces a raw `not implemented` from `QueryFramesInto`. Users who have the `sqlExpressions` feature toggle enabled will therefore get three different and non-actionable errors, two of which look like a malformed-query problem rather than "this feature is disabled". A single, explicit message such as "SQL expressions are disabled" in all paths would avoid support confusion.

findings.title: No regression test asserting SQL expressions are rejected
findings.body: This PR is a security fix that disables an RCE/LFI-capable code path, but no test is added. Nothing locks in the new behaviour, so a later refactor of `enableSqlExpressions` or of `pkg/expr/sql/db.go` could silently re-enable SQL expressions. Tests should cover both entry points: `ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery` with `QueryTypeSQL` (with the `sqlExpressions` toggle both on and off) must return an error, and `UnmarshalSQLCommand`/`NewSQLCommand` must fail rather than construct a usable command.

findings.title: tablesFromAST indexes ast[0] without a length check
findings.body: `flatten.Flatten(ast[0], ...)` will panic with an index-out-of-range if `ast` unmarshals to an empty slice (e.g. if `RunCommands` ever returns `"[]"`). Today the new stub always returns an error so this is unreachable, but the function is still exported-by-use and the DuckDB-specific `json_serialize_sql` command construction in `TablesList` (line 25) is now dead code against a stub that cannot execute SQL. Either guard `len(ast) == 0` or strip the now-meaningless parser/DuckDB SQL generation so it cannot be reintroduced as a live path.

findings.title: NoData result is immediately overwritten by TableData
findings.body: In `Execute`, the `if frame.Rows() == 0 { rsp.Values = mathexp.Values{mathexp.NoData{...}} }` assignment is unconditionally overwritten by the following `rsp.Values = mathexp.Values{mathexp.TableData{...}}`, so the empty-result branch has no effect and an empty frame is always reported as table data. This is pre-existing and currently unreachable (the stub DB always errors), but since the file is being touched it is worth either fixing with an `else`/early return or deleting along with the rest of the now-dead execution body.
